Re-checked on every run by design-lab/scripts/verify_contract_bindings.py: a BINDING row's named producer/consumer must still exist and still contain the declared version string, and an INERT row must state what is actually true rather than describing unimplemented work as pending. Paths are repo-relative; instance and test refs are path:line.

status_vocabulary.INERT: nothing in src/ produces or consumes this shape; the row says what exists instead

route_kind_vocabulary.SCHEMA_LESS: no schema validates this payload; the reason states why, and a version-bearing row must state the debt outright

Re-bound 2026-10-08. The route no longer answers with the bare receipt document: it answers with the design-lab/delivery-receipt-readback/v1 envelope, whose `receipt` member is that document returned verbatim and whose new members resolve each deliverable's rollback reference against the asset ledger. The document is not extended, because it signs its own bytes with receipt_sha256; the resolution therefore travels beside it, and this row binds the envelope schema and the emitter that writes its version. Both still hold: NativeDelivery.readback() reaches the same _load() that delivery_receipt.loads() re-verifies on every read, and test_delivery_evidence_ui_contract.py pins that the envelope carries the stored document rather than a rebuilt one. The two refusals keep their own codes: 404 DELIVERY_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND means no receipt was recorded for this ACTIVE version, 409 DELIVERY_RECEIPT_UNVERIFIED means a stored document contradicts its own bytes and the service will not certify them.

Paid 2026-10-22 (backend D, for Stitch screen D08). The list read now answers the shared design-lab/task-readback/v1 envelope: it names its own 100-row page size, says whether it truncated and gives the cursor from the same comparison (the contract refuses truncated=false next to a cursor, and refuses an empty page claiming truncation), carries the attempt-state words out of design-lab/config/state-vocabularies.json instead of re-typing them, and states the operation-level truth the code actually holds -- those words exist only as literals at the job_store._op() write sites, so the payload lists what this page observed rather than a closed list nobody declared. Two claims in the old row were wrong and are corrected here rather than carried forward: it cited design-lab/schemas/status-vocabulary, which is not a file in this repository (the vocabulary contract is the config above, guarded by design-lab/scripts/verify_state_vocabularies.py), and cancel.acknowledged is reachable -- job_store.acknowledge_cancel sets it on a CANCEL_REQUESTED attempt and moves the state to RECONCILING with the note 'adapter acknowledged cancellation; readback still required' -- so the envelope says what the flag asserts (the adapter confirmed the cancellation) and what it never asserts (the host stopped, or the artifact was reconciled).

Debt paid 2026-10-08 by section 30 and 31 of docs/audits/DESIGNLAB-LAUNCH-REVIEW-PREFLIGHT-2026-10-08.md: the projection answered two questions -- integrity (are these bytes still where the receipt says they came from) and currency (does this receipt still describe the bytes we are running) -- and nobody outside reporting.py could read either, so the evidence link of the chain was visible only to the code that wrote it. evidence_readback.projection() recomputes project_ledger over THIS checkout from the ledger and the object database (never from reports/current/, which is bound to whatever commit it was generated at) and validates its own payload, so a renamed key, a new reason token registered in code but not in the schema, or a record field leaking into the readback answers a named 500 instead of a short record a reader would call 'no evidence problems'. The reason vocabularies are two closed enums because the two questions are not the same question, and `current` is a subset of `verified` by construction -- the totals carry both counts and a test asserts that relation on the live payload.

It refuses both directions, and it refuses a pending number for a surface the row admits it never opened. The counts are not re-derived: prompt-result states come through the same _state_of predicate the prompt-result read-back uses, and the candidate counters come out of that resource's own read-back. The POST half is still this dispatch's honest gap: the creation echo {'project': {id, name, created_at}} carries no schemaVersion, so it is named here rather than counted as bound by the GET half.

DL-KB-02. Import identity is sha256(sourceId + "\x00" + version), so the same source and version land on the same entry id: re-importing identical bytes answers DUPLICATE with no write, the same version with different bytes answers 409 KNOWLEDGE_IMPORT_VERSION_CONFLICT, and a different version of the same source is kept beside the others as VERSIONED. A hand-created entry carrying the same source and version under a different id is reported as CREATED with an explanation that says the library now holds two records of that version -- calling it VERSIONED would claim a new version exists when one does not. source.verification stays UNVERIFIED: an import writes a record, it does not fetch or check the source.

DL-KB-02, extended 2026-10-24 for DL-KB-05 D5. The readback is where the screen's four states come from, computed by the service rather than the view: saved (this readback exists), provided (the current revision carries a creative), chosen (a named human adopted a revision), externally_verified (const false -- no route dispatches an external step). `reference_status` re-reads every pinned reference at its live revision: CURRENT means the bytes are still the ones the plan recorded, CHANGED means the object moved on, and `analysis` reports ANALYZED only when a stored reversal exists for that exact asset digest -- a reference registered as a link stays LINKED_ONLY, which is the measurement DL-KB-08's image state depends on. `current` is the stored document via $ref, not a re-render.

DL-KB-12, 「新版本不覆盖历史；对比页读的是两份真实修订」. The readback above serves only the NEWEST revision's document -- its `revisions` rows carry a digest, a created_at and an author, and nothing else -- so the stored body of an older revision was unreadable through every route and a comparison page could only restate hashes or guess the old text. This row binds the read that returns one row's own bytes: `document` is the stored JSON served verbatim, $ref-ed to design-lab/schemas/assistance-plan-v1.schema.json (the contract the write path validated those bytes against when they were filed) rather than restated here, and `content_sha256`/`created_at`/`created_by` are THIS row's columns while `latest_revision` and `is_latest` say where the plan has since moved -- so two calls that return the same document are a visible defect rather than the quiet bug. `is_chosen` is computed by the one query the readback's `choice` is built from (assistance_plan._choice_row), not by a second rule about a Human Gate record. There is no query string by design: the revision number is a path segment matched against the raw target, so `?revision=2` is a 404 rather than a parameter this route would pretend to honour, and `revisions/0` never reaches the store at all. Each refusal keeps its own code instead of collapsing into one generic error: unknown project 404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, a plan that is not in this project 404 ASSISTANCE_PLAN_NOT_FOUND, a number no row carries 404 ASSISTANCE_PLAN_REVISION_NOT_FOUND naming the plan id and the highest revision that does exist, an unparseable `document_json` 409 ASSISTANCE_PLAN_REVISION_UNREADABLE because the service does not hand back a guessed version, and a row whose published digest no longer covers its own bytes 500 ASSISTANCE_PLAN_REVISION_BYTES_MOVED -- the discipline of PLAN_FEEDBACK_BYTES_MOVED, since serving those bytes anyway would put one revision's digest beside another revision's words. What is deliberately NOT claimed: this is a read of stored history, so it reports no run, no send, no delivery and no model execution and declares no field that could imply one; the plan's four-state block stays the readback's single answer instead of being copied into a second envelope that could drift; and `reference_status` is not recomputed here, because whether a pinned reference has moved is a statement about the plan read today and must not silently rewrite what a 2026 revision said it used.

DL-KB-07. The collection lists each plan at its newest revision with the one sentence a reader needs to pick one: objective, output type, author, reference count, whether a creative was provided, and which revision a human chose (null until someone does). The query is named in the route pattern -- the same reason /api/knowledge-entries keeps search on its own path -- so one ledger row describes one document; offset/limit are parsed inside the handler, and a malformed number answers ASSISTANCE_PLAN_OFFSET_INVALID / LIMIT_INVALID rather than being silently ignored. next_offset is null on the last page, and an unknown project is 404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.

DL-KB-08. The initial screen must offer an output type before any workspace exists, so this read is deliberately project-independent: the project-scoped list route answers 404 until a project is created, which would leave the first plan unsaveable. The six values and their Chinese labels are the same table the create route validates against, served from the store's OUTPUT_TYPES/OUTPUT_LABELS rather than hand-copied into the view -- a second copy in TypeScript could offer a word the service refuses, and the page would only find out on submit.

DL-KB-07. Choosing is a Human Gate record, not a preference toggle: the route refuses actor_kind other than 'human' with 409 ASSISTANCE_PLAN_CHOICE_NOT_HUMAN, the table repeats the rule as a storage CHECK so the rule survives an application bug, and a revision outside the stored range is 400 CHOICE_REVISION_INVALID. The answer is the same readback the GET route serves, so the state the page shows after choosing is not a second envelope that could disagree. A second choice on the same revision is 409 ALREADY_CHOSEN: the record is a statement, not a switch.

DL-KB-11. The handoff material a plan produces on the way out: markdown, plain text, structured JSON and the 分镜 CSV, all four rendered from ONE builder (plan_export._intent) so 'the three exports agree' is a property of the code rather than of three hand-copied templates -- the schema's allOf block also ties each format word to the content_type and the filename extension a reader actually receives, because a mismatched pair is the shape a page cannot detect from the text. Every answer carries the revision it exported with that revision's content digest, the pinned reference snapshot copied from the stored document (an export freezes what the plan claimed; whether an object has since moved is the readback's reference_status, and an export may not quietly restate today's bytes), the emitter contract version, and an explicit not-executed statement. `sent`, `executed` and `external_verified` are `const false` in this contract: there is no outbound transport in this repository, so a download is a file in the designer's own folder and no flag can turn it into a delivery -- the exported bytes likewise never print 已发送/发送成功/delivered/模型已执行, which design-lab/tests/test_plan_export.py reads all four formats to prove. The route writes nothing and leaves the plan's four states byte-identical, and its two refusals are the point rather than edge cases: 409 PLAN_EXPORT_NO_SHOTS when the 分镜 CSV would be an empty table dressed as a storyboard (the reason `shots` had to become stored, validated, digest-covered data first -- an optional field added to assistance-plan/v1, so a plan stored before it existed still validates, and the create/revise routes accept the key without demanding it), and 400 PLAN_EXPORT_FORMAT_REQUIRED/_INVALID so an unnamed or unknown material keeps its own code instead of a 404 that reads like a deleted plan. A shot row filed under an output type that has no 分镜 is refused where it is written (409 ASSISTANCE_PLAN_SHOTS_NOT_APPLICABLE), so no plan can reach this route holding rows its own type disowns. Spreadsheet formula cells are handled by stating the rule to the reader, not by rewriting what a person typed: every field goes through csv.writer untouched (RFC4180 quoting, CRLF, leading BOM) and a 镜头说明 containing a quote, a comma or a newline is proven to survive the round trip.

DL-KB-09/10. The closed vocabulary the selection panel builds its selects from: the seven identity axes (07 line 29) and the thirteen capability fields (02 line 64), the five provenance kinds, the four support states, the five entry kinds and the nine validation dimensions. It is project-independent and served from the store's own constants because a hand-copy in TypeScript would be a second table that can offer a word the service refuses. `measured_fields` travels with it so the 「本项目未测试」 column is a number read from the service rather than a label the view decided.

DL-KB-09. The registry: five seeded profiles served read-only from the tracked config plus any draft a person wrote. The two histograms are part of the contract, not decoration -- the panel separates 官方支持 from 本项目未测试 using them, and PROJECT_MEASURED is 0 here because this round runs no external product or model. offset/limit are parsed in the handler and refused loudly (TARGET_PROFILE_FILTER_MALFORMED / LIMIT_INVALID) instead of failing inside the contract check, which would report a caller's typo as a defect in the registry.

DL-KB-09. One profile document, byte for byte what the config carries or the draft stored: a seeded id is derived from its own profile_key (never minted), a draft id is the one the create route wrote. Every field keeps its own provenance, an UNKNOWN keeps the reason it is unknown, `executable` is const false and `external_run_record` is const null. An unknown id is 404 TARGET_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND saying a profile is either a seeded config row or somebody's draft, so no caller can read a miss as "unsupported".

DL-KB-09, deliverable「用户可添加草稿档案，标未验证」. `stored: true` claims only that the bytes are in the state database. The route accepts the seven axes plus actor, source_ref and fields -- anything else is refused, so a draft cannot invent a column -- support_state is not settable (the table CHECK pins USER_DRAFT), and an absent source_ref becomes the literal UNUSED rather than an id this service minted. Writing PROJECT_MEASURED is 409 TARGET_PROFILE_MEASUREMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE: a measurement needs a run record bound to a real call and a readback, which no draft can supply. claims_not_made carries the denials on the answer itself.

DL-KB-09, acceptance B3. Input validation against what the profile's own fields say: DOCUMENTED_NOT_SUPPORT keeps a documented incompatibility in the vendor's words (FLUX.2 has no negative prompt) instead of smoothing it into silence, and UNKNOWN keeps its reason. A verdict never grants executability -- `grants_execution` is const false on every verdict and `executable` const false on the answer -- so no caller can read a validation as a go-ahead, and the fallback field travels with the answer because the honest output of an unreached entry is planning material, not a payload.

DL-KB-16, 「方案与适用经验可再次查找复用」. Every report recorded for one plan, oldest first, with the histogram computed from the same rows the page lists and `latest` a pointer into them: history is served whole rather than merged into one current value, because 「在 Meshy 里可用」 and 「在 Meshy 里不可用」 are both facts someone may need later and a merged field would erase the correction trail. `externally_verified` is a constant false for the collection -- reading reports back never verifies an external run. offset/limit are parsed in the handler and refused loudly (PLAN_FEEDBACK_FILTER_MALFORMED / LIMIT_INVALID / OFFSET_INVALID) rather than failing inside the contract check, which would report a caller typo as a defect in the registry.

DL-KB-16 acceptance 「反馈不得覆盖草稿/材料准备等独立状态」. A voluntary report. Outcome is one of the three words declared in design-lab/config/state-vocabularies.json and checked against plan_feedback.OUTCOMES in both directions by verify_state_vocabularies.py; there is no UNKNOWN outcome because not recording is the absence of a row, and sent/delivered/executed are not outcome words here since the service has no outbound transport. The actor is a named human (the table CHECK pins actor_kind), an absent source_ref becomes the literal UNUSED rather than an id minted here, and `revision` is required because a report is about the material somebody actually took away. `plan_states_unchanged` is a constant true and the plan readback still answers externally_verified=false afterwards: a satisfied report is somebody's word about an external tool, not the system confirming a run. Refusals: 400 OUTCOME_INVALID / REVISION_INVALID / FIELD_NOT_IN_CONTRACT, 404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND / ASSISTANCE_PLAN_NOT_FOUND, 409 REVISION_NOT_FOUND.
